competences: The learner identifies key facts about the executive.
The learner explains information about The President, ministers and civil servants using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes executive, president, ministers.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about the executive.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about The President, ministers and civil servants.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about the executive.
materials: Primary Five SST reference on The President, ministers and civil servants
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces the executive. They ask "Who was the first non executive president of Uganda?" and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about the executive
steps.content: The president is the chief executive officer in Uganda. He appoints top officials of the government eg. Ministers, Prime minister, Vice president, ambassadors, chief justice, RDCs etc. These appointed officials are approved by the parliament The president and all the ministers are referred to as the cabinent. It is headed by the president. It implements laws. Groups of people that make up the executive organ Ministers are appointed by the president and approved by the parliament Apart from the president, give one other group of people that makes up the executive. The president was given more power than before. A republic is a country governed by its own laws with the president as the head of state.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the executive on the chalkboard, including "The president is the chief executive officer in Uganda.; He appoints top officials of the government eg. Ministers, Prime minister, Vice president, ambassadors, chief justice, RDCs". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about the executive
steps.content: This organ is head by the president To provide social services People who belongs to the Executive The vice president The main duty of the executive is to implement government policies /programmes. It never gave the president executive powers Give the importance of governing a country using a constitution He was the first president of Uganda. He had no executive powers.(the executive powers were under the prime minister) His vice president was Sir Wilberforce Nadiope. He became the first executive president of Uganda.

steps.content: Who was the first non executive president of Uganda? | Name the first vice president of the non executive Uganda? | Name the first executive president of Uganda. | Who was the first president of Uganda in 1963? | Name the president who abolished kingdoms in Uganda in 1967?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "Who was the first non executive president of Uganda?" and "Name the first vice president of the non executive Uganda?". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on the executive, asks "Who was the first non executive president of Uganda?" and follows up with "Name the first vice president of the non executive Uganda?". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "Who was the first non executive president of Uganda?" and "Name the first vice president of the non executive Uganda?", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "What enabled Obote to become the first Executive Prime Minister of Uganda?"
